leftEvidence.title: The voice identifies the beloved Son

points.label: Divine action
points.left: A bright cloud overshadows Jesus, Moses, and Elijah; the voice repeats beloved Son language and commands the disciples to listen to him.
points.right: Jesus addresses “my God” in abandonment, cries again, dies, and is followed by torn curtain, earthquake, opened tombs, and the centurion’s confession.

points.label: Human response
points.left: Jesus shines; Peter proposes three shelters; the disciples fall afraid and later see Jesus alone.
points.right: Bystanders misunderstand the cry; the centurion and guards fear and name Jesus God’s Son.

payload.posture: The mountain voice names the beloved Son; at the cross the Son cries to “my God” in abandonment.

rightEvidence.title: Jesus cries to God and dies

payload.tension: Public affirmation and felt abandonment stand within the same Gospel’s account of Father and Son.
payload.title: The Father’s delight and the Son’s abandonment cry
